newsitem.title: RUSSIA: OLYMPICS-YELTSIN WEIGHS IN BEHIND PETERSBURG BID.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-YELTSIN WEIGHS IN BEHIND PETERSBURG BID.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday threw his considerable political weight behind St. Petersburg's bid to stage the 2004 Games, telling the International Olympic Committee all Russia wanted "a just decision".

Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told reporters Yeltsin had sent a message to IOC president Juan Antonio Samaranch just three days ahead of the announcement of a shortlist of five host cities from the 11 contenders.
"St. Petersburg's bid for the Olympics is a bid from all Russia," he said. "We are hoping for a just and unbiased decision on who is to be among the finalists. All Russia is very interested in this."
Yeltsin, 66, is a keen sports fan who devoted much of his youth to volleyball and played tennis before his recent heart trouble restricted his activities.
Russia says holding the Olympics in its baroque tsarist capital would be an international stamp of approval of its move to democracy and has applied heavy political pressure.
On Monday, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin telephoned Samaranch, who was once Spanish ambassador to Moscow, and told him St. Petersburg "can and should" stage the Games.
The IOC will announce the shortlist in Lausanne on Friday and give its final choice on September 5.
Rome and Athens are among the front-runners to host the Games.
